claims.text: The proposed framework separately models lattice and electronic heat transport.
The framework incorporates atomistic local lattice distortions.
The framework incorporates oxygen or other impurity scattering.
The framework will predict HfNbTaTiZr thermal conductivity within ±20% of experiment.
The framework will reduce prediction error by at least 50% relative to traditional approaches.
The target sample is single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with a controlled impurity level near 1 wt.% oxygen.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr has measured total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K·m) from 300 to 1200 K.
Local lattice distortions and impurity defects modulate phonon lifetimes.
Local lattice distortions and impurity defects modulate electron mobility independently of their effects on phonons.
Assigning distinct scattering mechanisms to phonons and electrons permits separate calculation of lattice and electronic thermal conductivity.
Disorder and impurities reduce lattice thermal transport in the target alloy.
Debye-temperature and standard DFT approaches oversimplify HfNbTaTiZr transport by conflating lattice and electronic contributions.
Traditional approaches have produced significant deviations from HfNbTaTiZr thermal-conductivity measurements.
The model will reproduce the temperature-dependent balance between lattice and electronic heat transport.
The framework is restricted to well-characterized, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with controlled impurity levels.
The framework will be less reliable for non-equilibrium or multiphase microstructures with nonuniform disorder.
The 50% improvement estimate is based on comparative error margins reported for conventional models.
Sample quality and oxygen content can affect observed model accuracy.
Failure to reduce error by at least 50%, or failure to capture distinct temperature-dependent lattice and electronic trends, falsifies the hypothesis.
